questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always been fascinated by Australia and wished to have a lot of time to explore the country, its culture and history. It was also important for me to speak the language of the people of the country I was going on exchange to, so that integrating and connecting with the locals would be easier.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was an incredible experience overall. a really good personal challenge and adventure.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: University of Melbourne felt a bit overwhelming at first, but they have loads of helpfull resources and staff to make it easier.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to Stop 1, where I was met by some very helpfull and sweet people, who could help me with receiving all the information I needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Due to the size of the university, it did feel a bit overwhelming, and it was important to take the initiative to go to social events and onboarding. The University didn't encourage these things particularly.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I looked at Airbnb with a friend who I was going with, and we found a good one for the entire of our stay. A lot of people used Flatmate and the Facebook group Fairyfloss. It was surprisingly easy. Would recommend staying in Fitzroy, Carlton, or Brunswick. Some people also just booked an Airbnb for the first 2 weeks and then went apartment hunting, which I heard was really easy and a good way to get to know the neighbourhoods before deciding where to live.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is really nice to live a bit away from campus, so you also see more of the city in everyday life, and transportation in Melbourne is really cheap.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was easy and a smooth process

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop 1 can help you with everything basicly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted. You can also make your own schedule, which I would recommend doing as early as possible, as fewer time slots for classes are available later on.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can make your own schedule, which I would recommend doing as early as possible, as fewer time slots for classes are available later on. I put all my classes on Monday and Tuesday, which was the best decision, cause it allowed me to go on longer trips. You can also watch lectures online, which gives a lot of freedom.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The classes were easier than at the University of Copenhagen. Felt kinda like gymnasium classes. Exams were easy to pass, but getting good grades still took work.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different from UCPH. The professors made a lot of fun (sometimes a bit strange) activities in the classes. Encouraged a lot of student participation and class discussions. Most of the time, there wasn't a PowerPoint in the class; it was just us and the professor talking. It could seem a bit unstructured and random at times.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introductory Macroeconomics
Terrorism: Shifting Paradigms (did not enjoy this one. Would not recommend) 
Global Intersections: Gender, Class, Race
Authoritarian Politics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Authoritarian politics were really interesting and relevant for current times. 
Global intersections gave really good perspectives, and the teaching format was very enjoyable.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I travelled a lot during my exchange and after, and did some expensive activities (diving, skydiving, Uluru trip, etc.), which I would really recommend, but it was definitely these trips that made the exchange expensive. The living cost in Melbourne was very comparable to living in Copenhagen, if anything, maybe a bit cheaper for food, transportation etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out is way cheaper than in Denmark, so that was really enjoyable. Sushi is cheap and a big part of the culture for some reason. However, alcohol (except for boxed wine) is very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of opportunities. Would really recommend attending the events at the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The University of Melbourne is very diverse, which is also shown in the incredible amount of student clubs available. They also have really good athletic clubs and facilities. The pool is free in the morning, and a lot of fitness classes are free as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the wine club, the underwater club (cheap diving!!) and the Arts students club. Would really recommend getting involved, as the classes themselves aren't that social unless you really try hard to make friends there.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go explore the different neighbourhoods of Melbourne. Drink coffee, go to cafes, little shops and museums. The city is so vibrant and has amazing vibes. I would also recommend taking some trips around the country or planning a longer trip after the semester. I went to Sydney, Cairns (Great Barrier Reef), Uluru, Great Ocean Road, Western Australia and Tasmania. I did most of the trips during the semester, and I regret not spending more time being in Melbourne, so I would recommend doing most of these things after the semester. I also joined a running club, which was a fun way to meet locals who were looking to socialise and make friends. A lot of people also went to New Zealand and Fiji (would recommend!!)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Australians are generally very helpfull and outgoing, so it felt very safe and welcoming when I first got to Australia.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I was surprised by how few exchange students were in my classes. It was mostly just local or international students, but a lot of them had busy lives with work and didn't seem to be looking for friends in the classes. I would recommend taking a lot of initiative and being outgoing, as most people in the classes didn't really socialise. It is also fun to attend events that the clubs organise.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I honestly found it easy. Danish and Australian humour are very similar. The most challenging part was how anti-social the classes were. Most classes are 40 minutes once a week, so there is very little time for socialising and making friends. I did manage to make friends in class, but it took a lot of initiative and awkward moments being the only people talking in a classroom of 25.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are very chill and laidback people, which was lovely to experience. They also love small talk in public, which felt really nice and comforting when arriving in a country alone.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take initiative, use the social opportunities the university provides and don't live on campus if you want a local experience, as most of the people living on campus are first-year international students, and I heard it was surprisingly anti-social.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It was overall the most incredible experience. I think experiencing the nature of Australia, the amazing, vibrant and diverse culture of Melbourne, and the very liberating freedom of being on exchange was extremely rewarding. Showing up alone in a new country, so far away from Denmark and building a life there felt very rewarding, freeing and of course also scary in a good way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The amount of opportunities was a bit overwhelming at times. Deciding where to put my energy and look for friends was probably the most difficult part of the exchange, but it just took some time before it worked out.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
